source.author: ArtIsWar
source.videoTitle: I Built a New Engine for MW4 | Free Warzone & DMZ Audio Guide

game.title: MW4 V1 (Warzone, DMZ)
game.note: Built for Warzone. Works in DMZ. Multiplayer is less consistent (Ninja perk, constant chaos).

styles.name: Theater Clear
styles.text: The game's own mix with footsteps brought forward. Quiet moments stay quiet, far sounds stay far, deep bass is held back so steps sit in a cleaner space. Calm around gunfire and explosions.

styles.name: Theater Clear+
styles.text: Theater Clear pushed harder: footsteps about 3 to 4 dB further out with a fast, hard edge. Other sharp sounds jump out too and rapid gunfire can flutter.

styles.name: Classic LE
styles.text: The old Loudness Equalization feel, rebuilt and cleaner. When you fire, only the front and your own gun come down, so the world stays present.

styles.name: Classic LE+
styles.text: Classic LE with footsteps pushed harder: each step's attack stands out about 2 to 3 dB more, while the room, your own steps and your gun sit about 3 dB lower.

styles.name: Classic LE Raw
styles.text: Classic LE with the world left alone: room tails, explosions and the echo of your own gun come through as the game mixed them.

styles.name: Classic LE Raw+
styles.text: Raw with gun levels that each make a real difference: from High down, the echo of your own shots is cut along with your gun.

guns.name: Ultra Low
guns.text: Your own gun at its quietest. What most people want.

guns.name: High
guns.text: Just a light touch on your gun.

guns.name: Extra High
guns.text: Your gun about as loud as the game mixed it (the old Stock).

heads.name: KU100
heads.text: The default head model. Start here.

heads.name: KEMAR
heads.text: The head these tunes were tuned on. Try it if front/back or high/low sounds do not place right for you.

gameSettings.name: Master Volume
gameSettings.why: The tune is built for 100. Turn loudness down in Voicemeeter, never here or in the Windows volume mixer.

gameSettings.name: Effects Volume
gameSettings.why: Same as Master: the tune needs full signal.

gameSettings.name: Game Sound Device
gameSettings.why: The tune only lives on this device. Anything else plays stock audio.

gameSettings.name: Speaker Output
gameSettings.why: Never 7.1. Windows Default lets the game send all 16 channels.

gameSettings.name: Enhanced Headphone Mode
gameSettings.why: It forces the game into stereo and breaks the tune.

gameSettings.name: Audio Mix
gameSettings.why: The tune was built around this mix.

gameSettings.name: Mono Audio
gameSettings.why: Mono collapses everything into one speaker.

gameSettings.name: Asymmetrical Hearing Compensation
gameSettings.why: It changes the signal before the tune and breaks it.

gameSettings.name: Reduce Tinnitus Sound
gameSettings.why: Softens the harsh high end a little.

gameSettings.name: Voice Chat Output Device
gameSettings.why: Keeps teammates' voices out of the tune so they sound natural.
